recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. No follow-up is needed for FHIR-7907 unless the work group wants a new, separate policy change to RESTful naming conventions.
issue_request: FHIR-7907 was a Published/Persuasive DSTU1 FHIR-core change request asking for documentation of why RESTful interactions and parameters use leading underscores, including _history, _search, _format, _count, and _since.
initial_application: The Jira comment records SVN revision 5534. The corresponding git-svn commit 4f363ad0bd1afafaa97da59cb1cee0d469fcf2ef included "#7907 - explain RESTful special characters" and added the underscore guidance paragraph to source/http.html. Later commits corrected typos and refined the wording without removing the applied explanation.
additional_context: The current source/http.html page says underscores disambiguate system-wide history/search from resource-type interactions, search/history interactions from resource instances, and all-resource search parameters from type-specific search parameters. The current source/search.html page separately describes underscore-prefixed search result parameters as result modifiers that are not SearchParameter resources. Searches of Jira, Zulip, and Confluence found no conflicting community record; later FHIR-50847 only removed the potentially misleading phrase "reserved names from other names" from the same sentence.
reconciliation: Published an empty no-change audit commit on the combined branch. The current source already provides the requested guidance, so adding more prose would be redundant rather than corrective.

related_jiras.note: A later commit clarified the same RESTful API sentence by removing "reserved names from other names" while preserving the FHIR-7907 underscore convention.
